newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says Italy in position to join EMU at start.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Italy in position to join EMU at start.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday that Italy was creating the conditions to join economic and monetary union (EMU) from its start in January 1999.

But he told the lower Chamber of Deputies at the start of a confidence debate that Italy needed political stability to get there and said his hard left ally, Communist Refoundation, had to fall into line.

"EMU is the primary objective of the government," Prodi said. He said the results of Italy's efforts to put its public finances in order were already being seen. "The country will be able to take part in EMU from the start," he said.
But he added that he was not ready to govern at any cost. "Italy needs stability (and) certainty," he said.

He said a rift with Refoundation, which emerged this week over policy towards Albania, was "so serious that we cannot continue without a strong, precise and clear clarification" of the terms of the partnership.
Prodi's centre-left government cannot survive in the lower house without the votes of Refoundation. It has said it will back the government in the vote, due on Saturday.
